text: As cities continue to grow, urban planners face the challenge of designing transportation systems that are both efficient and sustainable. In many large cities, congestion during rush hour has become a serious problem, with drivers stuck in traffic jams for hours every week. To reduce this problem, some governments have decided to expand their public transport networks, adding new routes and making them more accessible to everyone. Investing in infrastructure, such as new train lines and bus lanes, can also encourage people to leave their cars at home. If more citizens choose to commute by bicycle or on foot, cities become safer for both cyclists and pedestrians. In addition, using public transport instead of private cars helps lower emissions, which is important for fighting climate change. Some cities have introduced a low-cost fare system to make buses and trains a more attractive alternative to driving. Although building new infrastructure can be expensive, experts argue that it is a wise investment, since better transportation reduces pollution and saves commuters valuable time. Ultimately, a well-planned transport network benefits everyone, from daily commuters to visitors exploring the city on foot.
